original_content.knowledge_point: Finding the Rate of Change of a Function in a Given Direction
original_content.problem: Consider the function $f(x,y)=2xy+{e}^{3x-y}.$ What is the rate of change of $f(x,y)$ at the point $(1,3)$ in the direction in which the function decreases most rapidly?
original_content.worked_solution:
At a given point, a function $f(x,y)$ decreases most rapidly in the opposite direction of its gradient at that point.

In our case, we compute $-∇f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at the point $(1,3):$

$$
\begin{aligned}-∇\,f(x,y) & =-\frac{∂}{∂x}(2xy+{e}^{3x-y})\text{ }i-\frac{∂}{∂y}(2xy+{e}^{3x-y})\text{ }j \\  & =-(2y+3{e}^{3x-y})\text{ }i-(2x-{e}^{3x-y})\text{ }j \\ -∇\,f(1,3) & =-(2\cdot 3+3\cdot {e}^{3\cdot 1-3})\text{ }i-(2\cdot 1-{e}^{3\cdot 1-3})\text{ }j \\  & =-9\text{ }i-\text{ }j\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the rate of change of $f(x,y)$ at the point $(1,3)$ in the direction of $-∇f(1,3)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}‖-∇\,f(1,3)‖ & =‖-9\text{ }i-\text{ }j‖ \\  & =\sqrt{(-9)^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{82}.\end{aligned}
$$

corrected_content.problem: Consider the function $f(x,y)=2xy+{e}^{3x-y}.$ What is the magnitude of the rate of change of $f(x,y)$ at the point $(1,3)$ in the direction in which the function decreases most rapidly?
corrected_content.worked_solution:
Interpret the positive quantity calculated below as the magnitude of the rate of change in the direction of fastest decrease.

At a given point, a function $f(x,y)$ decreases most rapidly in the opposite direction of its gradient at that point.

In our case, we compute $-∇f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at the point $(1,3):$

$$
\begin{aligned}-∇\,f(x,y) & =-\frac{∂}{∂x}(2xy+{e}^{3x-y})\text{ }i-\frac{∂}{∂y}(2xy+{e}^{3x-y})\text{ }j \\  & =-(2y+3{e}^{3x-y})\text{ }i-(2x-{e}^{3x-y})\text{ }j \\ -∇\,f(1,3) & =-(2\cdot 3+3\cdot {e}^{3\cdot 1-3})\text{ }i-(2\cdot 1-{e}^{3\cdot 1-3})\text{ }j \\  & =-9\text{ }i-\text{ }j\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the magnitude of the rate of change of $f(x,y)$ at the point $(1,3)$ in the direction of $-∇f(1,3)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}‖-∇\,f(1,3)‖ & =‖-9\text{ }i-\text{ }j‖ \\  & =\sqrt{(-9)^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{82}.\end{aligned}
$$

Signed-rate note: $\nabla f(1,3)=(9,1)$ and the unit direction of fastest decrease is $\mathbf u=(-9,-1)/\sqrt{82}$. Therefore $D_{\mathbf u}f(1,3)=\nabla f(1,3)\cdot\mathbf u=-\sqrt{82}$. Its magnitude is $\sqrt{82}$, which is the positive quantity requested in the clarified study question.
